take01: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: one six-frame whole-figure 2D game animation key sheet on genuinely transparent background. Reference 1 is the exact Roshan drummer identity, polished painted storybook rendering, costume and pearl kit design; reference 2 is her mermaid identity/anatomy. Create ONLY one central lavender bass-drum strike action as SIX equal registered cells, 3 columns by 2 rows, reading left to right then down. Large native sheet, each cell at least 768 square; no labels, borders, captions or effects. Same orthographic camera, constant figure/head/hand sizes and absolutely fixed drum-kit fixtures in all six cells. Each cell is a COMPLETE new coherent drawing of the whole character plus same fixed kit, never independent limb pieces. Roshan has NO legs or feet. Show her visibly seated/supported on a low pearl stool behind the kit, with her rainbow tail curling to her right, clear of cymbal stand. Simplify the kit to teal left tom, lavender centre bass angled with a clearly visible playable top skin, gold star cymbal on right. The centre bass MUST be playable by a hand-held mallet, not a kick pedal. Exactly two arms/hands and two mallets. Preserve reference face, rainbow hair streak, costume and iridescent tail. Frames: 1 attentive ready, mallets just above drums; 2 whole-body anticipation: working mallet lifts, shoulders/hair/tail respond together; 3 downswing toward central skin; 4 crisp REAL mallet-tip CONTACT at central drumskin with a small visible depression at contact, wrist/shoulder/body follow-through; 5 clear rebound lifting mallet away, body/tail recover; 6 calm settled ready matching frame 1 support/pivot. Head and face remain clear; fixed drum hardware never travels or resizes. Preserve sharp painted hands, proper grips, clean contours, same body scale; no motion blur, ghost images, pasted limbs, floating player, camera zoom, ground/background/shadows painted behind alpha. Production pilot with readable physical contact, not six interchangeable poses. Keep ALL six complete figures/kits uncropped inside equally sized cells with generous transparent gutters.
take02: Use case: identity-preserve. Make one transparent RGBA sprite sheet for a complete seated mermaid bass-drum strike. Exactly FOUR equal square cells, 2 by 2; native sheet 1536 by 1536 or larger. This is the second and last pilot take. Each cell shows the ENTIRE Roshan plus kit at exactly the same fixed size and registered position. Reference1 locks her painted face, brown hair with rainbow streak, coral jacket, iridescent mermaid tail and pearl instruments. Reference2 locks her mermaid anatomy. No background pixels of any kind: truly empty alpha, no brown gradients, no drop-shadow field. Kit: same teal tom at left, lavender bass with its top drumskin angled upward for a hand mallet in the centre, gold star cymbal at right; pearl stool visibly supports her tail. No legs/feet, kick pedal or unseen hand. Four coherent full-figure drawings in reading order: A ready, B anticipation with HER LEFT HAND (viewer right) lifting its mallet and shoulders/hair/tail counterbalancing, C HER SAME LEFT HAND descending to clear genuine mallet-tip contact on the centre lavender skin, a small skin depression and body follow-through, D that SAME left mallet rebounding back to ready while shoulders/hair/tail settle. Her other/right hand holds its own stick near the left tom in all frames, no exchange of hands. Both hands have correct fingers and grips. Constant head width, eyes, arms and hand size in all four drawings. Absolutely identical drum/seat/cymbal geometry and placement in all four; whole figure is newly drawn per frame, no separate limb cutouts, no pasted duplicates or crossfades. Generous clear gutters, every extremity fully inside its cell. Precise polished storybook painted rendering, sharp contours; no blur, letters, arrows, labels, panel borders or scenery. The action must read ready → same-hand lift → same-hand true contact → same-hand rebound. Do not change outfits, perspective, drum topology or anatomical scale between cells.
